about: Maintenance tasks from published manufacturer documents. Each quote, page and interval was checked against the document by a second reader on the date shown. The machine’s own manual comes first.

tasks.title: Replace the CNC memory backup battery
tasks.action: Replace the control unit’s lithium memory-backup battery once a year, even without a BAT alarm. Back up the CNC data first. Section 3.10 of the manual has the steps and part numbers.

source.locator: 3.10 Replacing the memory backup battery in the control unit, pp. 270–271
source.quote: For this reason, FANUC recommends that the battery be replaced once per year regardless of whether a battery alarm is issued.
source.asStated: once per year regardless of whether a battery alarm is issued

tasks.title: Replace the absolute Pulsecoder (APC) batteries
tasks.action: Replace the batteries that keep the axes’ absolute positions. Batteries built into the amplifier (A06B-6114-K504) last about a year per three axes; a separate case of D cells (A06B-6050-K061) about two years per six axes. Change them with the power on and the machine in emergency stop, or the positions are lost.

source.locator: 4.7 Replacing battery for absolute Pulsecoders, 4.7.1 Overview, p. 316
source.quote: In general, replace the batteries periodically within the service life listed below. - A06B-6050-K061 or D-size alkaline dry cells (LR20) : Two years (for each six-axis configuration) - A06B-6114-K504 : One year (for each three-axis configuration)
source.asStated: A06B-6114-K504 : One year (for each three-axis configuration); A06B-6050-K061 or D-size alkaline dry cells (LR20) : Two years (for each six-axis configuration)

tasks.title: BAT alarm: replace the CNC memory battery
tasks.action: BAT blinks on the screen when the memory-backup battery runs low. Replace it as soon as possible, normally within a week; if the voltage keeps falling, the CNC memory is lost.

source.locator: 3.10, p. 270 (the BAT flag: 1.4 CNC state display, p. 45)
source.quote: When the battery voltage falls, alarm message "BAT" blinks on the LCD screen and the battery alarm signal is output to the PMC. Once the alarm message starts blinking or the alarm signal is output, replace the battery as soon as possible. In general, the battery can be replaced within one week of the alarm first being issued.
source.asStated: as soon as possible … within one week of the alarm first being issued

tasks.title: APC battery alarm (DS0306, DS0307, DS0308): replace the APC batteries
tasks.action: DS0307: the absolute Pulsecoder batteries are low. Replace them with the power on, normally within one to two weeks. DS0306: the voltage reached zero and the axis positions are lost; replace the batteries or check the cable, then return the axes to their reference positions. DS0308: the voltage was low at some point, even while the machine was off; replace the batteries.

source.locator: 4.7.1 Overview, p. 316; Appendix A alarm list, p. 678
source.quote: When alarm 307 (alarm indicating the voltage of the battery becomes low) occurs, replace the battery as soon as possible. In general, the battery should be replaced within one or two weeks, however, this depends on the number of Pulsecoders used.
source.asStated: as soon as possible … within one or two weeks

tasks.title: FAN warning or OH0701: replace the control unit fan
tasks.action: FAN blinks when a fan on the CNC control unit slows down; OH0701 means a fan stopped. Replace the fan motor as soon as the warning appears, with the power off. If the fan stops completely, the CNC stops on an overheat or system alarm.

source.locator: 3.11 Replacing a fan, p. 274; alarm OH0701, p. 565
source.quote: When a reduction in the speed of the fan motor is detected, the FAN warning message blinks on the LCD screen. When a failure such as stop of the fan motor is detected, an overheat alarm or system alarm is issued and the system stops operating. Therefore, as soon as the FAN warning appears, replace the fan motor.
source.asStated: as soon as the FAN warning appears

tasks.title: OH0700 (cabinet overheat): cool the CNC cabinet
tasks.action: The air around the CNC control unit is too hot. Bring the cabinet back to 0–58 °C (LCD-mounted unit) or 0–55 °C (stand-alone unit). The cabinet fans, filter mats and heat exchanger are the usual places to look.

source.quote: This alarm is issued if the ambient temperature of the CNC control unit is abnormally high. … Take appropriate action to the cabinet that houses the CNC control unit so that the temperature falls within the proper temperature range (0 to 58°C (for LCD-mounted type) or 0 to 55°C (for stand-alone type)).

tasks.title: Amplifier fan failure (DS0608–DS0611): replace the fan
tasks.action: A fan in a servo amplifier (DS0608, DS0609) or the power supply (DS0610, DS0611) has failed. Replace it: an internal-fan failure turns the servo off after one minute.

source.locator: Appendix A alarm list, p. 679; 8. Digital servo, p. 507
source.quote: DS0608 | SV COOLING FAN FAILURE | Internal agitating fan failure. DS0609 | SV RADIATOR FAN FAILURE | Radiator cooling fan failure. DS0610 | PS INTERNAL FAN FAILURE | Internal agitating fan failure. DS0611 | PS EXTERNAL FAN FAILURE | External radiator cooling fan failure.
source.asStated: on alarm (internal-fan warnings escalate after one minute)

tasks.title: Spindle amplifier fan failure (SP9056, SP9059, SP9088, SP9113)
tasks.action: A spindle amplifier or power supply fan has stopped. SP9056: replace the spindle amplifier’s internal fan. SP9088: its radiator fan. SP9113: the power supply’s external radiator fan. SP9059: the manual says to replace the power supply.

source.quote: SP9056 | COOLING FAN FAILURE | 56 | Replace the internal cooling fan. | The internal cooling fan stopped. … SP9088 | COOLING RADI FAN FAILURE | 88 | Replace the Spindle Amplifier radiator cooling fan. | The radiator cooling fan stopped.

tasks.title: Back up programs, offsets and parameters
tasks.action: FANUC says to back up regularly but gives no interval: set one that suits the shop. The control can also back itself up every so many days (parameter 10341).

source.locator: Safety precautions, p. s-5; 5.3 Automatic data backup, p. 330
source.quote: Back up the data (programs, offset values, and parameters) regularly. … When automatic data backup is performed periodically, this parameter sets the interval as the number of days.
source.asStated: regularly (no interval given); automatic backup interval set in days by parameter No. 10341

tasks.title: Preventive maintenance service (2,000 h or yearly)
tasks.action: FANUC’s checklist: replace the control cabinet filter mats; replace the CNC and Pulsecoder batteries; check the CNC, amplifier and spindle motor fans; check the central lubrication; service the air unit and dehumidifier; grease the tool changer; measure the tool pull-in force and spindle runout; inspect the way wipers, LM guides and ball screws; check geometry and level; back up programs and parameters; reset the maintenance counters. Periodical maintenance is for a FANUC-trained technician.

source.locator: p. 1 and the checklist on p. 2
source.quote: Maintenance intervals are adapted to the customer-specific, operational requirements after consultation (approx. every 2,000 operating hours or 1x per year).
source.asStated: approx. every 2,000 operating hours or 1x per year

tasks.title: Check inside the axis covers for chips
tasks.action: Look inside each axis cover and casting for chips every six months and remove any you find. Sweep chips out of the machine often.

source.quote: Sweep off chips from the inside of the machine frequently. Check the inside of each axis cover and casting for any chips semiannually. If chips are found inside any axis cover or casting, remove them.

tasks.title: Insulation (leakage) warning: have the motor and cable checked
tasks.action: The Robodrill watches the insulation of each motor and motor power cable. When it warns that the insulation is dropping, have that motor or cable checked or replaced before it fails.

source.quote: ● Leakage Detection Function ・Early detection of insulation resistance drop of each motor and motor power cable ・Enable preventive maintenance before breakdown

tasks.title: Preventive maintenance service (2,000 h or yearly)
tasks.action: FANUC’s checklist: lubricate all axes; check the safety equipment and collision protection; check the cooling fans (generator, CNC, amplifiers, pumps); clean the conductivity sensor; check and correct the levelling; service the automatic wire feeder and wire tension; deep-clean the upper and lower guide heads; check the work-tank door and arm seals; clean the float switch; service the wire take-off rollers; replace the cooler and CNC filter mats; replace the CNC and Pulsecoder batteries; back up all data including SRAM; inspect the motor and earth cables.

source.locator: p. 1 and the checklist on p. 2
source.quote: Maintenance intervals are adapted to the customer-specific, operational requirements after consultation (approx. every 2,000 operating hours or 1x per year).
source.asStated: approx. every 2,000 operating hours or 1x per year

tasks.title: Weekly cleaning
tasks.action: Clean the machine weekly. FANUC says it takes less than an hour; the machine’s maintenance guidance screen shows the steps.

source.quote: Easy Wire EDM Maintenance … Maintaining FANUC ROBOCUT only requires a few simple steps, with weekly cleaning taking less than an hour.
source.asStated: weekly cleaning taking less than an hour

tasks.title: Check consumable lives on the CNC screen
tasks.action: The ROBOCUT tracks the life of its consumable parts on its own consumables-management screen, and its maintenance guidance screen shows the daily maintenance with pictures. FANUC does not publish the default lives.

source.locator: p. 5 (printed pp. 8–9), Various functions to support daily maintenance
source.quote: Various functions to support daily maintenance … Consumables management … For monitoring the lives of consumable parts … Maintenance guidance … Provides the daily maintenance with pictures and drawings.
source.asStated: No interval stated; the CNC monitors consumable-part lives

tasks.title: Clean the conductivity sensor
tasks.action: Clean the conductivity sensor in the clean tank. It takes about 10 minutes.

source.quote: The conductivity sensor is located in the clean tank of the fluid system. … A conductivity sensor requires about 10 minutes to clean and should be done every 300 hours.

tasks.title: Clean the lower arm and head
tasks.action: Clean the lower arm and lower head, which collect dirt from being submerged. It takes about 15 minutes.

source.quote: The lower arm and head can accumulate excessive dirt from being submerged. … It takes about 15 minutes to clean these areas and should be performed every 500 hours.

tasks.title: Drain and refill the filter tank
tasks.action: Drain the filter tank, wipe out the sludge and refill it with DI water.

source.locator: Photo caption at the top of the article
source.quote: Avoid buildup of sludge and debris inside your filter tank by simply draining, wiping and refilling with DI water about every 1,000 hours.

tasks.title: Replace the power feed cables
tasks.action: Replace the cables that carry the cutting current from the power supply to the machine heads.

source.quote: Power feed cables bring the cutting current to the machine heads from the power supply. … It’s recommended that these be replaced every three years.

tasks.title: Conductivity too high: exchange the DI resin
tasks.action: When the machine warns that the water’s conductivity is too high, exchange the ion-exchange (DI) resin. It takes about 10 minutes.

source.quote: Resin exchange is required when the machine puts up a warning that the conductivity level is too high. Change time is only about 10 minutes.
source.asStated: when the machine puts up a warning that the conductivity level is too high

tasks.title: Check the coolant level
tasks.action: Check the coolant level each eight-hour shift, more often under heavy through-spindle coolant use. With an auxiliary filter, don’t fill the tank to the top at the end of the day: about 5 gal drains back overnight.

source.quote: 7.2 Daily Maintenance • Check the coolant level each eight-hour shift (especially during heavy TSC usage). NOTE: If your coolant system includes an auxiliary filter, do not completely fill the coolant tank at the end of the operating day. The auxiliary filter will drain approximately (5) gallons (19 liters) of coolant back into the coolant tank overnight.
source.asStated: Daily Maintenance: each eight-hour shift (especially during heavy TSC usage)

tasks.title: Check the lubrication tank level
tasks.action: Check the way-lube reservoir level on the lube panel and top it up with the oil named on the panel.

source.quote: 7.2 Daily Maintenance … • Check the lubrication tank level.

tasks.title: Clean chips from the way covers and bottom pan
tasks.action: Clear the chips off the way covers and out of the bottom pan.

source.quote: 7.2 Daily Maintenance … • Clean the chips from the way covers and bottom pan.

tasks.title: Clean chips from the tool changer
tasks.action: Clear the chips from the tool changer.

source.quote: 7.2 Daily Maintenance … • Clean the chips from the tool changer.

tasks.title: Wipe and oil the spindle taper
tasks.action: Wipe the spindle taper with a clean rag and apply a light film of oil.

source.quote: 7.2 Daily Maintenance … • Wipe the spindle taper with a clean rag and apply light oil.

tasks.title: Check the TSC filters
tasks.action: Check the through-spindle coolant filters; clean or replace them if needed.

source.quote: 7.3 Weekly Maintenance • Check the Through-Spindle Coolant (TSC) filters. Clean or replace them if needed.

tasks.title: Clean the coolant tank chip basket
tasks.action: Empty and clean the chip basket on the coolant tank: weekly on a machine with through-spindle coolant, monthly without.

source.quote: • On machines with the TSC option, clean the chip basket on the coolant tank. Do this monthly for machines without the TSC option.
source.asStated: Weekly on machines with the TSC option; monthly for machines without the TSC option

tasks.title: Grease the tool holder pull studs
tasks.action: Put a small amount of grease on each tool holder’s pull stud: weekly on a machine with through-spindle coolant, monthly without.

source.quote: • For machines with the TSC option, put a small amount of grease on each tool holder pull stud. Do this monthly for machines without the TSC option.
source.asStated: Weekly for machines with the TSC option; monthly for machines without the TSC option

tasks.title: Clean the exterior
tasks.action: Clean all exterior surfaces with a mild cleaner. No solvents.

source.quote: • Clean all of the exterior surfaces with mild cleaner. DO NOT use solvents.

tasks.title: Inspect and oil the way covers
tasks.action: Check that the way covers move freely; wipe them with light oil if needed.

source.quote: 7.4 Monthly Maintenance … • Inspect way covers for proper operation and lubricate them with light oil, if necessary.

tasks.title: Grease the tool changer guide rails
tasks.action: Put a small amount of grease on the outside edge of the tool changer’s guide rails, then run through all the tools.

source.quote: 7.4 Monthly Maintenance … • Place a small amount of grease on the outside edge of the guide rails of the tool changer and run through all tools.

tasks.title: Grease the tool holder V-flanges
tasks.action: Put grease on the V-flange of each tool holder.

source.quote: 7.4 Monthly Maintenance … • For machines with umbrella-style tool changers, put grease on the V-flange of each tool holder.

tasks.title: Clean the vector drive vents
tasks.action: Check the vector drive vents in the electrical cabinet (below the power switch) for dust. If there is buildup, open the cabinet, wipe the vents and blow the dust out with compressed air.

source.quote: • Check for dust buildup on electrical cabinet vector drive vents (beneath power switch). If buildup exists, open cabinet and wipe vents with a clean cloth rag. Apply compressed air as necessary to remove dust accumulation.

tasks.title: Check the spindle gearbox oil level
tasks.action: Check the oil level in the spindle gearbox.

source.quote: 7.4 Monthly Maintenance • Check the oil level in the gear box (if equipped).

tasks.title: Check the SMTC oil level
tasks.action: Check the oil level of the side-mount tool changer.

source.quote: 7.4 Monthly Maintenance … • Check the SMTC oil level (if equipped).

tasks.title: Replace the coolant and clean the tank
tasks.action: Drain and replace the coolant and clean the coolant tank thoroughly.

source.quote: 7.5 Every (6) Months • Replace coolant and thoroughly clean the coolant tank.

tasks.title: Inspect the hoses and lube lines
tasks.action: Check all hoses and lubrication lines for cracks.

source.quote: 7.5 Every (6) Months … • Check all hoses and lubrication lines for cracking.

tasks.title: Check the rotary A-axis lubrication
tasks.action: Check the rotary A axis and add lubricant if needed.

source.quote: 7.5 Every (6) Months … • Check the rotary A Axis, if equipped. Add lubrication, if needed.

tasks.title: Clean the lube panel reservoir oil filter
tasks.action: Clean the oil filter inside the lubrication panel’s oil reservoir and clean the residue out of the bottom of the filter.

source.quote: 7.6 Annual Maintenance … • Clean the oil filter inside the lubrication panel oil reservoir and clean out the residue at the bottom of the filter.

tasks.title: Replace the spindle gearbox oil
tasks.action: Drain and refill the spindle gearbox oil.

source.quote: 7.6 Annual Maintenance • Replace the gearbox oil (if equipped).

tasks.title: MAINTENANCE DUE icon: the control’s own timers
tasks.action: The Classic control keeps its own maintenance timers (Current Commands, Maintenance page; Settings 167–186). When the icon shows, do that item and reset its timer on that page.

source.quote: MAINTENANCE DUE | A maintenance procedure is due, based on information in the MAINTENANCE page. Refer to page 49 for more information.
source.asStated: when the MAINTENANCE DUE icon is displayed

tasks.title: Alarm 124 Low Battery: replace the memory battery
tasks.action: Replace the control’s 3.3 V lithium memory battery within 30 days of the alarm, or programs, parameters, offsets and settings can be lost. The alarm shows only at power-on. Keep backups until it is done.

source.quote: 124 | Low Battery | Memory batteries need replacing within 30 days. This alarm is only generated at power on and indicates that the 3.3 volt Lithium battery is below 2.5 volts. If this is not corrected within 30 days, you may lose your stored programs, parameters, offsets, and settings.
source.asStated: Memory batteries need replacing within 30 days (alarm shown at power-on)

tasks.title: Alarm 121 Low Lube or Low Pressure
tasks.action: Refill the way-lube tank and check that the lube lines are not blocked.

source.quote: 121 | Low Lube or Low Pressure | Way lube is low or empty or the lube pressure is too high or low. Check tank at rear of mill and below control cabinet. … Check that the lube lines are not blocked.

tasks.title: Alarm 120 Low Air Pressure
tasks.action: Check that the shop air gives at least 100 psi and that the machine’s regulator is set to 85 psi.

source.quote: 120 | Low Air Pressure | Air pressure dropped below 80 PSI for a period defined by Parameter 76. The LOW AIR PR alarm will appear on the screen as soon as the pressure gets low, and this alarm appears after some time has elapsed. Check your incoming air pressure for at least 100 PSI and ensure that the regulator is set at 85 PSI.
source.asStated: when alarm 120 occurs (air below 80 PSI for the time set by Parameter 76)

tasks.title: Alarm 151 Low Thru Spindle Coolant
tasks.action: Check the coolant tank level, the filters and the intake strainer for clogging, and the coolant lines for kinks.

source.quote: 151 | Low Thru Spindle Coolant | For machines with Through the Spindle Coolant only. This alarm will shut off the coolant spigot, spindle and pump, and purge the system. Check for low coolant tank level, any filter or intake strainer clogging, or for any kinked or clogged coolant lines.

tasks.title: Alarm 179 Low Pressure Transmission Oil
tasks.action: Check the spindle transmission oil level and its lines.

source.quote: 179 | Low Pressure Transmission Oil | Spindle coolant oil is low or low pressure condition in lines.

tasks.title: Check the control cabinet cooling unit
tasks.action: Check that the fan in the control cabinet’s cooling unit runs (a strong draft means it does) and that the outside air inlet is not blocked. Clean a blocked inlet with compressed air.

source.locator: Safety precautions 6 (11), periodic inspection of the control enclosure, p. P-(v)
source.quote: Inspect the following points every three months. - Is the fan motor inside the cooling unit working? The motor is normal if there is a strong draft from the unit. - Is the external air inlet blocked? If it is blocked, clean it with compressed air.

tasks.title: Check the oil-air lubrication oil level
tasks.action: Check the oil in the oil-air lubrication tank every morning before starting, and top it up with clean oil.

source.locator: 2-1 Supplying oil to the oil-air lubrication unit, p. P-44
source.quote: Check the oil amount every morning when starting operation.

tasks.title: Clean the oil-air lubrication pump filter
tasks.action: Clean the pump filter inside the oil-air lubrication tank.

source.locator: 2-1 Supplying oil to the oil-air lubrication unit, p. P-44
source.quote: Clean the pump filter in the tank every 6 months and change every year.

tasks.title: Replace the oil-air lubrication pump filter
tasks.action: Replace the pump filter inside the oil-air lubrication tank.

source.locator: 2-1 Supplying oil to the oil-air lubrication unit, p. P-44
source.quote: Clean the pump filter in the tank every 6 months and change every year.

tasks.title: Change the spindle head cooling unit oil
tasks.action: Change the oil of the spindle head cooling unit every 2,000 hours of operation: about every 10 months at 200 h a month, or every 4 months at 500 h a month.

source.quote: Every 2000 hours of operation: | 10 months when operated at 200 hours/month | 4 months when operated at 500 hours/month
source.asStated: Every 2000 hours of operation: 10 months when operated at 200 hours/month; 4 months when operated at 500 hours/month

tasks.title: Clean the cooling unit’s air filter
tasks.action: Clean the cooling unit’s air filter. A dirty filter cuts the cooling sharply and trips the compressor’s protection.

source.locator: 4-2 Cleaning the air filter, p. P-58
source.quote: Clean the filter once in two weeks. Negligence of periodical cleaning of the air filter will decrease the cooling effect considerably and activate the air compressor protective function.

tasks.title: Clean the way covers and wipers
tasks.action: Clean the sliding covers and wipers and check that the wipers move smoothly. Replace a wiper whose sealing edge is cracked or worn.

source.locator: 7-1 Sliding cover and wiper, p. P-61
source.quote: Clean them every six months. ... Replace the wiper with new one if any damage such as a crack or abrasion can be observed in the sealing surface.

tasks.title: Replace the door safety window
tasks.action: Replace the door’s safety window every two years: coolant slowly weakens it, until it may no longer stop flying chips or parts.

source.quote: The safety window glass must be replaced every two years. Safety window glass performance gradually deteriorates due to coolant corrosion.
